fields.description:
## Context / Problem

Most plan-review criteria have no eval fixture, so a rubric edit ships with no behavioral
oracle. Before any fixture can be written, something has to decide WHICH observed reviews
are trustworthy evidence of a criterion's correct behavior — and the corpus records what the
reviewer said, not what was true.

Two hazards make naive selection wrong. Reviewer noise: 551 consecutive review pairs over
byte-identical material flipped verdict 208 times, so a label taken from one observation
flips under that same noise. Prompt vintage: rubrics were rewritten repeatedly inside the
corpus window and `plan_review_verifier.md` last changed 2026-08-11, so a finding from a
retired rubric does not describe today's criterion — and nothing cohorts by vintage, since
`regver` (`manifest.py:139-185`) hashes routing and criterion ids but not rubric bytes.

The material itself is committed and free to read: manifest
`docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/replay/corpus-2026-08-30.manifest.json` records 6,482
sidecar rows, `verified_count` 6,202, and `plan_replay/corpus.py` reconstructs each row's
at-review plan text (`corpus.py:270-288`).

## Approach

An offline selector that reads the corpus and writes a LABELED CANDIDATE MANIFEST — one JSON
document listing, per criterion, each candidate with its direction, its tier, the signals
that support it and its rank. It emits no YAML and issues no model call, so it is cheap to
re-run while its rules are tuned, and the manifest is directly inspectable as the answer to
"which criteria have minable signal, and how strong is it".

**Candidate key and signal join.** A candidate is keyed by `(criterion, norm_id)`
(`sidecar.py:656,663`); signals join on that key across a ticket's review sequence. This is
load-bearing because the signals live on different pair relationships: `labels.py` computes
`finding_survival` only over consecutive DIFFERING-material pairs, while reproduction
consensus is defined over EQUAL-`material_fingerprint` pairs. The selector reads consensus
from the equal-fingerprint reviews carrying the key, and author-response from the first
differing-material pair following the last of those. A key present in only one relationship
gets only that signal.

**Vintage gate.** A review is eligible for criterion C only when `review_event_ts`
(`corpus.py:273`) postdates the last `origin/main` commit touching C's resolved prompt file:
a project `.rebar/prompts/<prompt-id>.md` override when present, else packaged
`src/rebar/llm/reviewers/<prompt-id>.md`. A criterion whose resolved file has no committed
history — a `project.`-prefixed overlay criterion, or a new rubric — FAILS the gate and is
skipped, since no review can postdate a commit that does not exist. A signal read from the
Pass-2 vector additionally requires postdating `plan_review_verifier.md`.

**Label signals**, offline and independent of the reviewer's own verdict:
- *Reproduction consensus* — the key fired, or stayed absent, consistently across two or more
  reviews with equal `material_fingerprint`. The only signal valid in the no-fire direction.
- *Author response* — `finding_survival == "resolved_by_author"` (`labels.py:158-171`), the
  only per-finding label the labels module produces. Fire direction only.

**Escaped defect is a PRIORITY signal, not a label.** `labels.py:70-73` derives
`escaped_defect` from a ticket's `close_class` and inbound `caused_by` links — a per-TICKET
bool with no criterion attribution, so labelling a per-criterion case with it would seed a
must-fire candidate under an unrelated criterion. It only raises a review's selection rank.
Its absence never evidences correct silence, so `clean_close` (`labels.py:43`) is not a
no-fire source either.

**Tiered bar.** A FIRE candidate is BLOCKING only when all four hold: reproduction consensus,
author-response corroboration, `abs(decision_margin)` (`sidecar.py:344-367`) at or above the
constant `MIN_MARGIN = 0.15`, and the vintage gate. The margin and author-response conjuncts
are per-finding and exist only in the fire direction, so a NO-FIRE candidate reaches at most
ADVISORY, on consensus plus the vintage gate. Any single signal plus the gate proposes
ADVISORY. The margin constant drops findings close enough to `block_threshold` that a small
perturbation flips them — the population that makes a fixture flaky.

**Rank order.** Candidates rank BLOCKING before ADVISORY, then by escaped-defect priority,
then by descending `abs(decision_margin)`, then ascending `review_event_uuid`
(`corpus.py:273`) as a total tie-break. The manifest records that rank so the sibling emitter
can take a fixed number per side deterministically.

**Skip list.** A criterion with an open ticket titled `unreliable-criterion: <criterion-id>`
is skipped and appears in the manifest with a zero candidate count and that reason.

## Scope

A new module under `src/rebar/llm/evals/` holding the selector and its predicates, consuming
`plan_replay/corpus.py` and `plan_replay/labels.py`, plus the manifest writer. It covers only
criteria `criteria.effective_routing('.', gate_key='plan_review')` reports having no spec
under `.rebar/evals/` or `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/`.

## Non-goals

- Writing any `.eval.yaml`; the sibling emitter owns spec serialization and its schema.
- Admitting a candidate; the admission runner owns that.
- Any model call.
- Per-finding true/false-positive labelling or human adjudication.

## Testing

Unit tests over the selection predicates on synthetic corpus rows, plus one integration test
over the real committed corpus with no model configured. Every assertion is deterministic.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A review timestamped before its criterion's resolved prompt commit is excluded and an
      otherwise-identical later one is included; verified by `pytest` asserting the manifest
      holds the second row's id and not the first's.
- [ ] A criterion whose resolved prompt file has no committed history is skipped; verified by
      `pytest` asserting a `project.`-prefixed criterion carries a zero candidate count.
- [ ] A candidate whose only signal is `escaped_defect` appears in no direction, while a
      candidate carrying it ranks above an equal-signal peer without it; verified by `pytest`
      asserting the candidate list and the two rank positions.
- [ ] A key present only in equal-fingerprint pairs records reproduction consensus and no
      author-response signal; verified by `pytest` asserting the recorded signal set.
- [ ] Each blocking conjunct, removed one at a time from a fire candidate, downgrades it to
      `advisory`, and the all-present case yields `blocking`; verified by parameterized
      `pytest` over the recorded tier string.
- [ ] A no-fire candidate never reaches `blocking`; verified by `pytest` asserting the tier
      is `advisory` for a no-fire candidate holding reproduction consensus.
- [ ] Given 6 qualifying candidates on one side with distinct margins, the recorded ranks
      follow the stated order; verified by `pytest` asserting the rank sequence.
- [ ] A criterion with an open `unreliable-criterion: <id>` ticket carries a zero candidate
      count and that reason; verified by `pytest` with a stubbed ticket listing.
- [ ] Two consecutive real runs over the committed corpus emit a byte-identical manifest;
      verified by `diff` of the two files exiting 0.
- [ ] The selector completes with the repository's network guard active; verified by `pytest`
      running it under that guard.

## Definition of Done

`make lint`, `make typecheck` and `make test` pass; the real-corpus run writes a manifest
covering every uncovered criterion; the diff touches nothing under `.rebar/evals/` or
`src/rebar/llm/reviewers/`.

## Budget

**$0.** Selection is a pure function of the corpus and git metadata.
fields.title: Select and label per-criterion fixture candidates from the plan-review sidecar corpus
